words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. desid. √ji

hindi: माने हुए सन्धि-पण के उद्वेग को करने वाले को जीतना चाहने वाला बलवान्, जहाँ से अपनी भूमि और अपनी सेनाओं की अपनी ऋतु की वृत्ति हो, और शत्रु दुर्ग-रहित अपसार वाला, पार्ष्णि-रहित और आसार-रहित हो, वहाँ से चढ़ाई करे।
english: The strong one desiring to conquer [the one] causing agitation [by] the permitted treaty-stipulation should march from there, from where [there are] one's own ground and the course of one's own season for one's own troops, and [where] the enemy [has] a retreat that is no fort, [has] no rear and no reinforcer.

text_flags.why: possible stray dot: śatruḥ and apārṣṇiḥ are two separate words (nominative subject and its adjective), not a compound

notes: The first compound anujñāta-sandhi-paṇa-udvega-karam is obscure: taken as accusative object of vijigīṣamāṇaḥ ('desiring to conquer [him who] causes agitation over a permitted treaty-stipulation'); alternatives: a different reading of paṇa (bargain, stake) or of anujñāta (permitted, assented to). sandhi = treaty (Book 7). adurga-apasāra: taken as 'whose retreat is no fort'; alternative 'without fort and without retreat'. apārṣṇi: 'without a rear'; alternative 'without a heel-seizer' (pārṣṇi-grāha). sva-ṛtu-vṛtti: 'course of own season' is literal, i.e. the season suiting one's own troops. ca after anāsāra joins the last items. yāyāt = should march.

hindi: विपर्यय में प्रतिकार किया हुआ चढ़ाई करे।
english: In the reverse [case], with the remedy made, [he] should march.
notes: viparyaya = reversal, i.e. the contrary of the conditions of unit 1; the word 'case' is supplied in brackets. pratīkāra = remedy (glossary).

hindi: साम और दान से दुर्बलों को झुकाए, भेद और दण्ड से बलवानों को।
english: By conciliation and gifts he should make the weak bow down; by dissension and force [he should make bow down] the strong.
notes: The verb is not repeated in the second clause; it is supplied in brackets. upa-√nam caus. is taken literally ('make bend/bow'); the sense is bringing to submission. daṇḍa as upāya = force.

words.gloss: with none between and with one between

hindi: और उपायों के नियोग, विकल्प, समुच्चय से अनन्तर और एक के अन्तर वाली प्रकृतियों को वश में करे।
english: And by the niyoga (restriction), vikalpa (option) and samuccaya (combination) of the means he should bring under control the constituent elements [that are] with none between and with one between.
notes: anantara-eka-antarāḥ is read as a dvandva 'with none between / with one between' (the neighbouring and the next-but-one); the doubt is whether it is a dvandva or a single compound. prakṛti = constituent element (glossary); it may here mean the neighbouring kings/states. sādhayet (caus. √sādh): 'bring under control'; alternatives 'accomplish', 'subdue'. ca joins this sentence to the preceding one ('and').

words.gloss: protection of village [and] forest dependants, cattle-station, merchant-route

hindi: “ग्राम-अरण्य-उपजीवी, व्रज, वणिक्-पथ का पालन और त्यागे हुए, भागे हुए, अपकारियों का अर्पण” — सान्त्व का आचरण करे।
english: “Protection of village [and] forest dependants, cattle-stations [and] merchant-routes, and the handing over of [those] abandoned, fled [and] doing harm” — he should practise conciliation.
notes: The first compound is ambiguous: upajīvin ('living on') may attach to grāma and araṇya only (dependants of village and forest) or to all following members; kept literal. ujjhita = abandoned, apasṛta = fled/withdrawn, apakārin = doing wrong/harm. arpaṇa = handing over (alternative: giving back). iti closes the description and is carried by the quotation marks. sāntva = conciliation (glossary).

words.gloss: gift of land, property [and] a maiden

hindi: “भूमि, द्रव्य, कन्या का दान और अभय का” — दान का आचरण करे।
english: “Gift of land, property [and] a maiden, and of freedom from fear” — he should practise gift.
notes: kanyā = maiden (alternative: daughter). abhaya = freedom from fear/safety; 'and of freedom from fear' is elliptical for 'and the gift of freedom from fear'. dānam abhayasya ca is read as one list. iti closes the description (quotation marks).

words.gloss: of neighbouring chiefs, forest chiefs, members of his family [and] princes in disfavour
by the support of any one
request for treasury, army, land [and] share

hindi: “सामन्त, आटविक, तत्कुलीन, अपरुद्धों में से किसी एक के सहारे से कोश, दण्ड, भूमि, दाय की याचना” — भेद का आचरण करे।
english: “Request for treasury, army, land [and] share, by the support of any one of the neighbouring chiefs, forest chiefs, members of his family [and] princes in disfavour” — he should practise dissension.
notes: Glossary terms: sāmanta = neighbouring chief, āṭavika = forest chief, tat-kulīna = member of his family, aparuddha = prince in disfavour; upagraha = support. 'his' in tat-kulīna is not identified in the unit. dāya = share (alternatives: gift, inheritance). daṇḍa here = army. bheda as upāya = dissension. iti closes the description (quotation marks).

words.gloss: by the means of open, treacherous [and] silent fighting [and] acquisition of forts

hindi: “प्रकाश-युद्ध, कूटयुद्ध, मौन युद्ध, दुर्ग-लाभ के उपायों से अमित्रों का प्रग्रहण” — दण्ड का आचरण करे।
english: “Capture of enemies by the means of open, treacherous [and] silent fighting [and] acquisition of forts” — he should practise force.
notes: The compound can be divided differently: prakāśa, kūṭa, tūṣṇīm may each qualify yuddha (open battle, treacherous warfare, silent fighting), as taken here; tūṣṇīm-yuddha is taken literally (silent fighting). lambha = acquisition (glossary). pragrahaṇa = seizing/capture. daṇḍa as upāya = force. iti closes the description (quotation marks).

hindi: इस प्रकार उत्साह वालों को सेना के उपकारी स्थापित करे, अपने प्रभाव वालों को कोश के उपकारी, प्रज्ञा वालों को भूमि के उपकारी।
english: In this way he should station the energetic [as] helpers of the army, those having their own might [as] helpers of the treasury, the wise [as] helpers of the land.
notes: Double accusative (persons and their function) is read as apposition, with [as] supplied; alternative: two separate groups. sva-prabhāvavat: 'their own' is literal and the owner is not stated. daṇḍa = army; prabhāva = might (glossary). Whom he stations is not named; presumably those won over in the preceding units.

words.gloss: born from wares, towns, villages [and] mines
by gems, valuables, trifling [things] [and] raw materials
arisen from property, elephants, forest [and] cattle-station

hindi: उनमें से जो पण्य, पत्तन, ग्राम, खान से उत्पन्न रत्न, सार, फल्गु, कुप्य से, या द्रव्य, हाथी, वन, व्रज से उठे यान-वाहन से बहुत बार उपकार करता है, वह विचित्र भोग वाला है।
english: Of them, what [one] benefits many times by gems, valuables, trifling [things] [and] raw materials born from wares, towns, villages [and] mines, or by vehicle [and] mount arisen from property, elephants, forest [and] cattle-station — that [has] varied enjoyment.
notes: The attachment of the two participles is a guess: sañjāta with ratna-sāra-phalgu-kupya, samuttha with yāna-vāhana. yāna here = vehicle (not the Book 7 'march'). phalgu = trifling (alternative: weak, inferior). sāra = valuables; kupya = raw materials. bahuśaḥ: many times (alternative: in large quantity). citra-bhoga: 'of varied enjoyment/benefit'; likely a technical name for a kind of helper, kept literal; the subject of upakaroti is unstated. teṣām refers back to the helpers of unit 9.

hindi: जो सेना या कोश से बहुत उपकार करता है, वह महा-भोग वाला है।
english: What [one] benefits greatly by army or by treasury, that [has] great enjoyment.
notes: daṇḍa here = army (prakṛti sense). mahat as an adverb (greatly); alternatively 'a great [benefit]' as the object. See unit 10 on bhoga.

hindi: जो सेना, कोश, भूमियों से उपकार करता है, वह सर्व-भोग वाला है।
english: What [one] benefits by army, treasury [and] lands, that [has] all enjoyment.
notes: daṇḍa = army. See unit 10 on bhoga.

hindi: जो एक ओर से अमित्र का प्रतिकार करता है, वह एक ओर से भोग वाला है।
english: What [one] counteracts the enemy on one side, that [has] enjoyment on one side.
notes: pratikaroti: 'counteracts' (literal: does a counter-measure to); alternative 'checks, remedies'. ekataḥ = on one side (literally 'from one side'). The bahuvrīhi ekataḥ-bhogin is a neuter nominative in -i as printed.

hindi: जो अमित्र और आसार का दोनों ओर से प्रतिकार करता है, वह दोनों ओर से भोग वाला है।
english: What [one] counteracts the enemy and the reinforcer on both sides, that [has] enjoyment on both sides.
notes: āsāra = reinforcer (glossary 6.2 sense); alternative 'reinforcement'.

hindi: जो अमित्र, आसार, प्रतिवेश, आटविकों का सब ओर से प्रतिकार करता है, वह सब ओर से भोग वाला है।
english: What [one] counteracts enemies, reinforcers, neighbours [and] forest chiefs on all sides, that [has] enjoyment on all sides.
notes: prativeśa = neighbour (literally 'dwelling opposite/near'). The singular/plural of the first three members is not marked in the compound; the plural is taken from āṭavikān.

words.gloss: to be won over by a gift of land

hindi: पार्ष्णिग्राह और आटविक, शत्रु का मुख्य या शत्रु, भूमि-दान से साधने योग्य, कोई मिल जाए; गुणहीन भूमि से इसे ग्रहण कराए; असम्बद्ध से दुर्ग में स्थित को; जीविका के अयोग्य से आटविक को; पुनः ली जा सकने वाली से शत्रु के तत्कुलीन को; कटी हुई से शत्रु के अपरुद्ध को; नित्य शत्रु वाली से श्रेणी-सैन्य को; बलवान् सामन्त वाली से संगठित सेना वाले को; दोनों से युद्ध में प्रतिकूल को; जिसमें व्यायाम प्राप्त नहीं हुआ उससे उत्साही को; शून्य से शत्रु-पक्ष के को; क्षीण की हुई से अलग ले जाए गए को; महा-क्षय-व्यय-निवेश वाली से गए और लौटे हुए को; आश्रय-रहित से पीछे हटे हुए को; दूसरे से न बसाए जा सकने वाली से स्वयं ही भर्ता को ग्रहण कराए।
english: If any heel-seizer and forest chief, enemy's chief or enemy, to be won over by a gift of land, should be found: with a land without qualities he should cause him to take up; with [one] not connected, [the one] standing in a fort; with [one] not to be lived off, the forest chief; with a retakable [one], the enemy's member of his family; with a cut-off [one], the enemy's prince in disfavour; with [one] having permanent enemies, the guild troops; with [one] having strong neighbouring chiefs, [one] with united army; with both, [one] adverse in battle; with [one] whose activity is not obtained, the energetic [one]; with an empty [one], [one] of the enemy's party; with a weakened [one], the carried away [one]; with [one] having great loss, expenditure [and] settlement, the one gone and returned; with [one] without refuge, the one retreated back; with [one] not to be inhabited by the other, he should cause the master himself indeed to take up.

text_flags.why: likely typo: śūyayā is not a word; śūnyayā (empty, instrumental feminine) fits the pattern of land-qualities and the sense

notes: Structure: a series of 'instrumental feminine land-quality + accusative person', with 'bhūmyā' supplied from the first pair, so [land] is understood in the bracketed 'with [one]'. upagrāhayet (caus. upa-√grah) is literally 'cause to take up/accept'; the sense is 'win over, gain as a supporter' (alternative). sādhya = to be won over (glossary sense). Doubtful items: apratisambaddha (not connected, i.e. not adjoining), nirupajīvya (giving no livelihood), pratyādeya (retakable, glossary), apacchinna (cut off), saṃhata-bala (compact/united army), ubhābhyām (with both of the two preceding lands is presumed), alabdha-vyāyāma (vyāyāma = activity, glossary 6.2; alternative exertion), mahā-kṣaya-vyaya-niveśā (niveśa = settlement; alternative encampment), anapāśraya (without refuge), pareṇa anadhivāsyayā (not to be inhabited by the other = the enemy, 'the other' literal). bhartṛ = master (Book 7). svayam eva = 'himself indeed'. Lone '-' at the ends of lines 1 and 2 are continuation marks. tat-kulīna: 'his' is the enemy (śatroḥ).

hindi: उनमें से बड़े उपकार वाले और विकार-रहित का अनुसरण कराए।
english: Of them, [the one] of great help and [the one] without change he should cause to follow.
notes: anuvartayet (caus. anu-√vṛt): literal 'cause to follow/conform'; alternatives 'comply with, oblige'. Subject-less participles are shown with [the one]; the persons are those won over in units 9-16.

hindi: प्रतिकूल को गुप्त रूप से वश में करे।
english: [The one] adverse he should bring under control by secret [means].
notes: upāṃśu = in secret/quietly; kept as 'by secret [means]'. sādhayet as in unit 4 (alternative: overcome, dispatch). pratiloma = adverse (cf. unit 16).

hindi: उपकारी को उपकार-शक्ति से सन्तुष्ट करे।
english: The helper he should satisfy by power of help.
notes: upakāra-śakti is ambiguous: the power of help (of the helper) or ability in proportion to help; kept literal (śakti = power).

hindi: और प्रयास के कारण धन और मान करे, और व्यसनों में अनुग्रह।
english: And by reason of effort he should make wealth and honour, and favour in calamities.
notes: kuryāt = should make (i.e. bestow); the verb governs both artha-mānau and anugraham. artha here = wealth (glossary: plain wealth with māna). vyasana = calamity (glossary). prayāsataḥ: by reason of (the helper's) effort; the owner of the effort is not stated.

hindi: अपने आप आए हुओं का यथेष्ट दर्शन और प्रतिविधान करे।
english: Of [those] come of themselves he should make seeing as desired, and provision.
notes: darśana = seeing (audience/interview); pratividhāna = provision/counter-arrangement (alternatives: redress, remedy). yathā-iṣṭa = as desired (iṣṭa = desired).

hindi: और इनमें तिरस्कार, उपघात, निन्दा, अतिवाद का प्रयोग न करे।
english: And in these he should not apply contempt, injury, reproach [or] over-speaking.
notes: kutsa = reproach/abuse (stem form in compound); ati-vāda = over-speaking (glossary). 'In these' = in the case of the persons dealt with above (literal locative).

hindi: और अभय देकर पिता के समान अनुग्रह करे।
english: And having given freedom from fear, he should favour like a father.
notes: abhaya = freedom from fear (alternative: safety).

hindi: और जो इसका अपकार करे, उस दोष को प्रकट करके उसे खुले रूप से मरवाए।
english: And whoever should do wrong to him, having proclaimed that fault, he should have him killed openly.
notes: asya = 'to him' (the person won over in the preceding units); tad doṣam: tad is the sandhi form of tat before d, agreeing with the masculine doṣa. ghātayet (caus. √han) = cause to be killed. prakāśam adverbial: openly (cf. prakāśa-yuddha, open battle).

words.gloss: by reason of the others' agitation

hindi: या दूसरों के उद्वेग के कारण दाण्डकर्मिक के समान चेष्टा करे।
english: Or by reason of the others' agitation he should act like a dāṇḍakarmika.
notes: para-udvega-kāraṇa is ambiguous: 'for the reason that the others are agitated' or 'for the purpose of causing the others' agitation'; the literal 'by reason of' is kept. para = the other(s) (glossary: not 'enemies'). dāṇḍakarmika stays as a term (glossary; literally 'one engaged in punitive action').

hindi: और मारे गए के भूमि, द्रव्य, पुत्र, स्त्रियों को लक्ष्य न बनाए।
english: And he should not aim at the land, property, sons [and] wives of the slain.
notes: abhi-√man (middle) = set the mind on, aim at; alternatives 'covet', 'lay claim to', 'attack'. Rendered 'aim at' also in units 30 and 32. dāra is plural in sense (wives).

hindi: इसके कुल्यों को भी अपने पात्रों में स्थापित करे।
english: He should station even his kinsmen in [their] own offices.
notes: pātra literally 'vessel'; here taken as 'office/position' (alternatives: worthy places, fit recipients). sveṣu: 'own', owner not stated (presumably the kinsmen). kulya = kinsman (glossary).

hindi: कर्म में मरे हुए के पुत्र को राज्य में स्थापित करे।
english: He should station the son of [one] dead in action in the kingdom.
notes: karman = action; the sense 'in the course of the operation (campaign)' is likely but not stated. The identity of the dead man (the king who was slain/submitted) is not stated.

hindi: इस प्रकार इसके सेना सहित समर्पण करने वाले पुत्रों और पौत्रों का अनुसरण करते हैं।
english: In this way his [people] submitting with their army follow [his] sons [and] grandsons.
notes: daṇḍa-upanata = one submitting with his army (glossary). The word [people] and [his] before sons are supplied; asya is read as the conqueror. Alternative: asya = of the submitted king.

hindi: किन्तु जो उपनतों को मारकर या बाँधकर भूमि, द्रव्य, पुत्र, स्त्रियों को लक्ष्य बनाए, उसका उद्विग्न मण्डल अभाव के लिए उठता है।
english: But whoever, having killed or bound [those] submitted, should aim at [their] land, property, sons [and] wives — his agitated circle rises up for [his] non-existence.
notes: abhimanyeta: see unit 26. maṇḍala = circle (glossary). abhāvāya = for non-existence (i.e. for his destruction); 'his' before non-existence is supplied.

hindi: और जो इसके अमात्य अपनी भूमियों में आश्रित हैं, और वे इससे उद्विग्न मण्डल का आश्रय लेते हैं।
english: And [those] ministers of his who are dependent on [their] own lands, and they, agitated at him, resort to the circle.
notes: udvignā = udvignāḥ (visarga lost before m). asya with udvigna: 'at him' is a loose rendering of the genitive; alternative 'his [people]'. āyatta = dependent (on); sva-bhūmi: here 'own lands' of the ministers. maṇḍala = circle (glossary).

hindi: स्वयं या राज्य को या इसके प्राणों को लक्ष्य बनाते हैं।
english: Either they themselves aim at the kingdom, or at his life.
notes: svayaṃ vā … vā is ambiguous: 'themselves (aim at) the kingdom, or at his life' (taken here) or 'they aim at the kingdom or at his life by themselves'. asya is placed once but governs both rājyam and prāṇān. prāṇa is plural in form (vital breaths = life). abhimanyante: see unit 26. Subject (the agitated ministers of unit 31) is not stated.

hindi: और अपनी भूमियों में राजा इसलिए साम से रक्षित होकर राजा के अनुकूल, पुत्र-पौत्रों का अनुसरण करने वाले होते हैं।
english: And, therefore, the kings in [their] own lands, protected by conciliation, become favourable to the king, following [his] sons [and] grandsons.
notes: The first ca joins this unit to the preceding argument. rājñaḥ is read with anuguṇāḥ (favourable to the king); it may also govern putra-pautra (the king's sons and grandsons). tasmāt = therefore (alternative: from that). sāman = conciliation (glossary: sāma). The couplet is divided into two printed lines; one sentence.
